name: Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.isSafe_sum
summary: Components at different letters pair to zero (ζ acts on them by different Teichmüller lifts, whose difference is a unit), so the pairing of the sums is the sum of the diagonal pairings.

steps.claim: For every letter i: Σ_l wittPairing(P)(wittFst(u_l), wittFst(v_i)) is its term l = i, since the terms l ≠ i vanish:
steps.lean:
have Z i := Fintype.sum_eq_single i fun l n ↦ show P.wittPairing (wittFst _ (u l))
    (wittFst _ (v i)) = 0 from (isUnit_teichmuller_sub (Units.ext.mt n)).smul_eq_zero.1
    (by simpa [by simpa [mem_letterPart_iff_mulZeta] using h, sub_smul] using!
    (diagTensor_induction fun _ _ ↦ diagTensor_induction (by simp [mulZeta, modPairing]) : ∀ u v,
    P.wittPairing (wittFst _ (S.extLattice.mulZeta.wittMap u)) (wittFst _ v) =
    P.wittPairing (wittFst _ u) (wittFst _ (S'.extLattice.mulZeta.wittMap v))) (u l) (v i))

steps.claim: for l ≠ i, wittPairing(P)(wittFst(u_l), wittFst(v_i)) = 0: ζ acts on u_l by ω(l) and on v_i by ω(i), and the pairing is O-balanced: ⟨ζu, v⟩ = ⟨u, ζv⟩, because modPairing(P) is an O-bilinear form ψ on Y ⊗_O Y' followed by a Z_p-linear λ : O → Z_p and reduction mod p^m, hence Z_p-bilinear and O-balanced (it is not O-bilinear with values in Z/p^m(1), which has no O-action); so ω(l)·⟨u_l, v_i⟩ = ⟨ζu_l, v_i⟩ = ⟨u_l, ζv_i⟩ = ω(i)·⟨u_l, v_i⟩ (the Teichmüller lifts acting through W(C^♭)); ω(l) − ω(i) is a unit for l ≠ i (isUnit_teichmuller_sub).
steps.lean:
show P.wittPairing (wittFst _ (u l))
    (wittFst _ (v i)) = 0 from (isUnit_teichmuller_sub (Units.ext.mt n)).smul_eq_zero.1
    (by simpa [by simpa [mem_letterPart_iff_mulZeta] using h, sub_smul] using!
    (diagTensor_induction fun _ _ ↦ diagTensor_induction (by simp [mulZeta, modPairing]) : ∀ u v,
    P.wittPairing (wittFst _ (S.extLattice.mulZeta.wittMap u)) (wittFst _ v) =
    P.wittPairing (wittFst _ u) (wittFst _ (S'.extLattice.mulZeta.wittMap v))) (u l) (v i))

steps.claim: Hence p^κ⟨Σ_l u_l, Σ_i v_i⟩ = Σ_i p^κ⟨u_i, v_i⟩, a sum of elements of the submodule smallPart(m) (f).
